title: Standing to File and Appointment of Representative — Appeals and Grievances
content:
Standing and representation in Appeals and Grievances cases:

1. Only a party listed for the tier among those who may file has standing: the beneficiary, a parent or legal guardian of a minor or incapacitated beneficiary, an appointed representative, or — where the tier lets a participating provider file in its own right — a participating provider on its own denied claim.
2. A filing by an appointed representative proceeds to a decision only once an appointment of representative is on file for the case. Whether it is on file is read from the case record — the case's marker that an appointment of representative is on file, and the documents received for the case — not from the filer's say-so.
3. A missing appointment must arrive within the tier's appointment window of filing; when it does not, the case is dismissed as no representative appointment. A case under review is dismissed on that ground when the appointment never arrived within the window.
4. When an appointment of representative form is received for a case, the case is marked as having an appointment of representative on file.
5. A spouse is not a representative by marriage alone.
6. A sponsor may file for a minor child; an adult beneficiary's case is the beneficiary's own.

**Who is filing — judgement table**

| Filer | Standing | Before a decision |
|---|---|---|
| the beneficiary | yes | — |
| parent or legal guardian of a minor or incapacitated beneficiary | yes | — |
| sponsor, for a minor child | yes | — |
| appointed representative | yes | an appointment of representative must be on file for the case |
| spouse, by marriage alone | not a representative | — |
| participating provider, on its own denied claim | only where the tier allows a participating provider to file | — |

**Hypothetical case.** An appointed representative files a case on a tier with a 30-day appointment window, and no appointment is on file. If the appointment of representative form is received on day 12 after filing, the case is marked as having the appointment on file and may proceed to a decision. If no form has arrived when the 30 days have run, the case is dismissed as no representative appointment.
